content.text:
Yes. You can have each agent run on a different AI model/provider if you want. Here are practical ways to do it and what to consider.

What to decide first
- Which models/providers do you want per agent? (e.g., coder on a code-optimized model, OSINT on a faster/cheaper model, etc.)
- Do you want persistent per-agent model assignments, or only per-session overrides when a task runs?
- How do you want to handle costs, rate limits, and context/history across models?

Ways to configure per-agent models
1) Per-agent session when spawning
- Use sessions_spawn with a model override for each agent.
- Example approach:
  - coder: model=openrouter/coder-variant or a code-optimized model
  - social: model=openrouter/creative or a general-purpose chat model
  - osint: model=openrouter/fast-qa or a model tuned for research
  - generalist: model=openrouter/auto or a balanced model
- This keeps each agent isolated with its own model stack.

2) Per-agent persistent config
- Create a per-agent config (in MEMORY.md or a dedicated config file) that maps agent role -> model.
- When you start or spawn an agent, read that map and apply the model accordingly.
- Useful for long-running teams where agents stay active and you want consistency.

3) Hybrid approach
- Use a default/generalist model for most tasks, but override for specific tasks or tasks that require specialized behavior (e.g., coding tasks always route to coder-model; OSINT tasks route to an OSINT-optimized model).
- This gives flexibility without forcing every action to a different model all the time.

Practical steps to implement
- Decide and document your model map, e.g.:
  - coder: openrouter/coder-variant
  - social: openrouter/creative
  - osint: openrouter/osint-lite
  - generalist: openrouter/auto
- When spawning agents, pass the model parameter:
  - functions.sessions_spawn with parameters including model: "openrouter/coder-variant" (adjust to your actual model IDs)
- If you’re reusing existing agent sessions, you can:
  - Create dedicated sub-sessions for each agent with their model, and have Pluto coordinate tasks to the right agent session.
- If you need dynamic switching:
  - Provide a command to rebind an agent to a different model and reload its context.

Considerations and trade-offs
- Consistency vs cost: Different models may have different capabilities and costs. Align with each agent’s task requirements.
- Context bleeding: Different models may have different context windows; plan how you handle long-running tasks and history.
- Tooling and capabilities: Some models may be better for code (coders), others for research (OSINT). Choose accordingly.
- Governance: Document the model mapping so you can audit decisions and reproduce results.

Questions for you
- Do you want persistent per-agent models, or just per-task overrides?
- Do you already have specific model IDs or providers in mind for each agent?
- Should we implement a quick prototype with one or two agents first (e.g., coder on a code-optimized model, generalist on a balanced model), then expand?

If you want, I can draft a concrete config snippet and a small plan to test with your four agents.
